content.title: How To Create a Personal Brand (And Why It’s Important)
content.text: Career developmentHow To Create a Personal Brand (And Why It’s Important)Updated December 11, 2025What is a personal brand?Why do you need a personal brand?Benefits of a personal brandHow to create your personal brandA personal brand is a marketing strategy to promote yourself and your career. When creating your personal brand, you can consider your unique talents, skills and goals that distinguish you from your peers. Understanding how to create a personal brand can help you manage your professional image and market your skills and experiences to attract potential employers.In this article, we explain how to create a personal brand and how it's beneficial to your professional development.What is a personal brand?A personal brand is how others perceive your skills, talents and qualifications. It helps define who you are and what you hope to achieve in your career and industry. A personal brand reflects your professional values and work ethic. It's unique to you and is a vital part of your reputation in the workplace.Why do you need a personal brand?A personal brand helps you differentiate yourself from competitors. If you're an individual seeking a job, you can distinguish yourself from other potential candidates. A personal brand lets you promote your reputation and skills and attract potential employers through job-posting websites, social media and networking.Benefits of a personal brandWith a personal brand, you can:Promote yourself onlineA personal brand can help direct your networking activities on social media and improve your website. It's a marketing strategy that professionals refer to as digital branding. The internet is a powerful tool for connecting with employers. With a personal brand message, you can make more high-quality connections.Build trust and authorityA personal brand can help inspire trust from your audience and position you as an expert in your field. Recruiters on social media are more apt to find you and request your opinions as a thought leader in your industry. It positions you as an expert in a specific niche or field which can, as a result, attract potential employers.Present a compelling elevator pitchAn elevator pitch is a 30- to 60-second explanation of who you are and what you have to offer. Imagine being stuck in an elevator with the leader of a company for which you want to work. You only have until the doors open again to make your case. Having a good elevator pitch can help you refine your brand and be ready to use it when the opportunity is available.Related: How To Give an Elevator Pitch (With Examples)Improve your networking skillsIt can sometimes be challenging to promote yourself at a networking event. When you develop a personal brand, you can have the words you need to describe what you do clearly and effectively. Your brand can address who you are, what you do and how others can benefit from your skills or services. Being able to describe your accomplishments and goals while networking can help you make stronger impressions on prospective employers and professional contacts.Related: 10 Tips To Help You Network Like a ProAdvance your careerWhen you create a brand that centers on your professional goals, accomplishments and skills, you can better identify new opportunities to advance and develop. Written elements of your personal brand can serve as a reminder of your objectives as you search for a job, craft your resume and cover letter or prepare for an interview. You may also discover opportunities that you want to pursue that you hadn't previously considered.Read more: What Is Career Advancement? Definition and ExamplesHow to create your personal brandHere are some simple steps you can follow to create your own personal brand:1. Understand what your assets areAssets are a reflection of who you are, what you do and what your values are. Think about what makes you unique or specific things you can offer to employers. Some of your most important assets are your skills, which are things at which you excel. They can be hard skills that you acquired through education or job experience or soft skills such as personality traits. As you incorporate your skills into your personal brand, you may also consider what your passions are and how they relate to your skills.Other assets you may consider including are your credentials. Credentials are great additions to your personal brand, as they show your expertise and education in specific subject matter areas. For example, if you want to be a real estate agent, your real estate license is a clear asset. Some final assets to consider when creating your personal brand are your core values and beliefs. These beliefs determine how you work, and employers want to hire candidates who have values that align with the values of their company.2. Develop a brand messageA brand message consists of a few sentences and describes what you have to offer an employer, team or role. When creating your personal brand message, consider asking yourself questions like, "Why do I want to build a personal brand?" and "What characteristics do I want to associate with my brand?" Answering these questions may make it easier to create a concise and accurate brand message.Developing a brand message helps you clearly define your personal brand and have something concrete you can refer to when making decisions about your career. Write down a few sentences about why you're crafting a personal brand, how you want it to look and what outcomes you hope to achieve. You can keep this message to yourself for future reference or put it on your website or social profiles.Related: How To Create an Impactful Personal Branding Statement3. Craft a personalityA brand personality incorporates the key characteristics and traits of who you are as a professional. This can then help you decide on the general tone you want for your brand. Depending on what your career goals are, you may want to incorporate traits like "hard-working," "results-driven," "creative," "risk tolerant," "highly motivated" and "dependable."4. Target your audienceYour target audience is the group of people you want to see your personal brand. If you're trying to get a job, it could be employers in a specific niche. Identify who you want to target, and then use the characteristics of that audience to develop your brand. You may benefit from adjusting your target audience depending on what kind of company you're applying to and what kind of work environment it creates.Related: How To Talk To Recruiters5. Offer a solutionWhen crafting your personal brand, think about what your audience wants and find something specific to offer. Focus on the solution or services you can provide to meet the needs of your potential employer. To create your offer, think about not only what you do but also how you do it to demonstrate your unique perspective and thought processes. The information on this site is provided as a courtesy and for informational purposes only.
